title: Anthem Biosciences Ltd - 544449 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Anthem FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 2,124 crore (+18% incl. other income), with Q4 record revenue Rs 611 crore (+26% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA margin 48.1%.
summary.overview: Anthem closed FY26 with its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4, up 26% YoY to Rs 611 crore, with CRDMO up 31% and specialty ingredients up 8%. FY26 EBITDA reached Rs 990 crore (43.4% margin, +31%) and PAT Rs 592 crore (+31%), though full-year revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the company's stated 20% aspiration. Management said destocking by customers is largely behind it and refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance. Capex is shifting to Unit 4, with Phase 1 of about Rs 1,200 crore to finish by March 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth about 15% per CFO; total revenue incl. other income Rs 2,280 crore, +18%
Includes forex and RoDTEP gain Rs 63 crore and financial/other non-operating income Rs 92 crore
+130% YoY; includes Rs 98 lakh exceptional credit from Labour Code impact

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 1,773 crore (83% of total), +18%; Q4 Rs 513 crore, +31% YoY. Management split: commercial molecules about 60%, late-stage/Phase 3 development and manufacturing batches about 15%, R&D about 8-9%, with specialty ingredients the balance.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 352 crore (17%); Q4 Rs 98 crore, +8% YoY, the first revenue growth after flat first three quarters. Management aspires to around 20% growth; products include serratiopeptidase, vitamins, probiotics and enzymes, sold mainly to India and RoW markets.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 or FY28 guidance given; management aspires to around 20% growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, citing a 10-year revenue CAGR near 20%.
FY26 revenue growth was about 15% versus a 20% aspiration; management says EBITDA and PAT growth of 30%+ more than compensated.
EBITDA margin: asked whether 38-40% is a fair assumption, CFO said the company has delivered these levels and will continue to deliver, with operating leverage expected to hold margins steady.
Destocking is described as behind the company; management expects restocking to lift FY27 top and bottom line.
Biosimilar project expected to hit P&L next year (FY27) and would be classified under CRDMO.
Unit 3 expected to be EBITDA-positive this year; Unit 4 ready by next financial year per CEO closing remarks.
capex_capacity: Unit 4 is the largest project, with Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore across FY27 and FY28, targeted for completion in the latter half of March 2028.
Phase 1 adds about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis (vs current 425 KL) and 100 KL fermentation (vs current 180 KL), roughly doubling custom synthesis and adding about 50% fermentation capacity.
Capex guidance: about Rs 700 crore in FY27, then about Rs 500 crore per year after that (including maintenance).
Unit 2 expanded from 246 KL to about 376 KL (50% addition); Unit 3 fully operational, and more Unit 2/3 expansion sits in CWIP in H1 FY27.
Unit 4 has two further phases after Phase 1; Phase 1 at least doubles capacity and Phase 2 could triple overall size.
Unit 3 added lab space to handle more projects; management says the company can handle 200 projects versus 100 today.
demand_pricing: Management said destocking happened in FY26 across many customers, and restocking is now under way.
Orders are coming in for both chemistry and biology, with growth in peptides and RNAi (oligonucleotide) work.
Four commercial molecules went live in FY26 (one with big pharma, three with emerging biotechs); they contribute about 8-9% of revenue now, with a 2-3 year ramp expected.

Commercial pipeline rose to 14 molecules; Phase 3 pipeline stands at 10 molecules, all from emerging biotechs (four added in FY26, non-lateral), spanning ADC, peptides, oligonucleotides and biotransformation.

Two new direct big pharma relationships added in FY26; more than 100 early-stage R&D projects. Biotech funding up about 50% YoY through April (per CFO); early-stage requests rising in number though smaller in size.
Management sees tariffs as no impact so far, since commercial big pharma products have separate arrangements with the US administration.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 growth for CRDMO research and manufacturing be framed, and are destocking issues resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about 20%+ growth as per track record but gave no FY27 guidance; it says destocking is largely behind and restocking should benefit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for adding big pharma customers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Unit 2 expansion (246 to about 376 KL) and Unit 3 give headroom until Unit 4 comes online; capacity is not a constraint now.

qa_highlights.question: Capex outlook for FY27 and the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 700 crore in FY27 and about Rs 500 crore thereafter, with Unit 4 Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin improvement and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration into one intermediate was completed, improving material margins in Q3 and Q4 FY26; management expects 38-40% EBITDA margins to be sustained with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 3 pipeline composition?
qa_highlights.answer: All four Phase 3 additions were non-lateral, from the emerging biotech funnel; the basket of 10 spans ADC, peptides, oligos and biotransformation, with at least one molecule per modality.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the four newly commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about 8-9% of current revenue, with peak sales estimated four to five years after launch and a two-to-three-year ramp.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the 20% aspiration; management declined to commit to FY27 numbers.
Specialty ingredients growth is patchy because its capacity shares space with CRDMO; a dedicated facility in Unit 4 is planned.
Unit 4 capex execution (Rs 1,200 crore over FY27-FY28) and Phase 1 completion by March 2028.
Maintaining 38-40% EBITDA margins at high growth; management acknowledged inflationary pressures and the Middle East war as headwinds.
Ramp-up of the four newly launched commercial molecules; launch timing depends on partner filings and registrations across geographies.
GLP-1 generic opportunity depends on customer formulation approvals, with timing given as six to eight months; the company is in talks with big players to replace China-sourced APIs.
Q4 PAT includes a Labour Code-related exceptional credit of Rs 98 lakh.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and margins, but deliberately non-committal on FY27 and FY28 numbers, repeatedly declining explicit guidance. Answers on destocking, tariffs and biotech funding were reassuring, while peptide and ADC competitive questions were answered in general terms, with payload and competitor details withheld.
key_quotes: Historically, if you look at it last 10 years, our revenue growth has been around 20% level.
We want to refrain from giving any guidance for FY27 or FY28, but long-term, have we put in the ingredients from a growth point of view? I'd say that the answer is yes.
So, capacity is not a constraint for us now.
Unit 3 is already turning around and it's going to be in the positive territory this year.

growth.why: No FY27 or FY28 guidance given; management only restates a ~20% long-term aspiration (FY26 revenue grew ~15%), backed by Unit 2 expansion, Unit 4 Phase 1 (~Rs 1,200 cr over FY27-FY28, completion by March 2028), 14-molecule commercial pipeline and restocking after destocking, with Q4 revenue +26% YoY.
